thema_eingabe: "Free" AI tools fact-checked: what the free plans really include

skript.thema: Free AI tools fact-checked: what the free plans really include

teile.name: Promise
teile.text: Is free AI really free? Six official pricing pages, read October 9, 2026. Here's what each free plan actually includes.
teile.szene: Medium shot of a black-haired man in a black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses at a night desk, studying six glowing pricing cards, painted urban open-world poster style, bold ink contours, warm neon light.

teile.name: Looka
teile.text: Looka makes logos for free. The download is what costs. One low-res PNG is $35, one time. Multiple high-res file types cost $72.
teile.szene: Looka pricing page card showing free logo creation with Basic and Premium package prices.

teile.name: Leonardo
teile.text: Leonardo's free plan is $0 a month. You get 150 fast tokens per day. The catch: creations are public. Private access starts at $12 a month.
teile.szene: Leonardo.Ai pricing page card comparing the free plan with public creations and the Essential plan with private creations.

teile.name: Gamma
teile.text: Gamma gives 400 credits at signup. Each prompt can make up to 10 slides. Plus adds 1,000 monthly credits and removes Gamma branding.
teile.szene: Gamma pricing page card showing free plan credits, slide limit per prompt and the Plus plan.

teile.name: Suno
teile.text: Now the big catch. Suno's free plan gives 50 credits per day. But it has no monthly song downloads and no commercial rights. Commercial use starts with Pro.
teile.szene: Suno pricing page card showing free plan with 50 daily credits, no downloads, no commercial rights, and the Pro plan.

teile.name: ElevenLabs
teile.text: ElevenLabs is genuinely free for text to speech. You get 10k credits per month. But the commercial license starts at the paid Starter plan.
teile.szene: ElevenLabs pricing page card showing the free plan with 10k monthly credits and the paid Starter plan for commercial license.

teile.name: Notta
teile.text: Notta's free plan covers 120 transcription minutes monthly. Each conversation can run up to 3 minutes. Pro raises that to 1,800 minutes monthly.
teile.szene: Notta pricing page card showing free plan 120 minutes, 3 minutes per conversation, and Pro 1,800 minutes.

teile.name: Rule
teile.text: So here's the rule. Free to try isn't always free to publish. Check downloads, commercial rights and privacy first. Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Medium shot of a black-haired man in a black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses ticking a paper checklist at a city window at dusk, painted urban open-world poster style, warm light.

regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

For AI Tools Explained Shorts comparable to the approved 82-second pilot, aim for 14-18 distinct relevant motifs instead of the previous 12 across 23 shots. Reduce repeated identical imagery and add genuinely different demonstrations, details or illustrative actions supported by the narration. Zooms, crops and label changes do not count as new motifs. This is a planning target, not a retroactive rejection of the positively received pilot.

For Business Origin Stories the user's latest refinement on 2026-10-05 is to aim for about 24 shots with 18 distinct relevant motifs for comparable 90-second Shorts. The delivered 24-shot/14-motif video was positively received; 18 motifs is the next improvement target, not its actual delivered count. Reduce repeats by adding four genuinely different relevant subjects or actions. Preserve useful pacing and the original channel character. Do not count zooms, crops or label changes as new motifs; adapt other video lengths to their story.
Explicit viewer feedback about our videos (not source facts): Es wurden einfach viel zu wenig Fotos verwendet

Explicit viewer feedback about our videos (not source facts): Nutzerfeedback 08.10.2026 nach den ersten automatischen Videos: Bilder lebendig, warm und ausgefuellt, damit die Leute Lust haben zu schauen; alles gemalt im Open-World-Spielplakat-Stil (keine echten Spielfiguren), keine Stockclips. AI-Tools-Video (Whirl) hatte zu wenig Emotion, die Sprechgeschwindigkeit war gut.

Explicit viewer feedback about our videos (not source facts): Nutzerfeedback 09.10.2026 zum AI-Tools-Short Aurelio (1:10, Nutzernote 6/10): Die Videos nutzen Bilder, die nicht mit dem Text zusammenhaengen. Befund: 21 von 21 Einstellungen Symbol-Illustrationen (Sparschwein, Muenzen, Schluessel), obwohl die README ein demo.gif mit genau den genannten Funktionen hatte. Konkrete Werkzeug-Funktionen mit echtem Material (README-Bilder/Animationen) zeigen.

Explicit viewer feedback about our videos (not source facts): Nutzerfeedback 09.10.2026 zum Vorschaubild-Entwurf: Der Typ auf dem Bild hat 3 Haende (Anzug). Firma, Logo und Fabrik muessen groesser sein als der Typ; der Typ soll nicht im Vordergrund stehen, sondern immer das Logo, ueber das man die Geschichte oder das KI-Tool erzaehlt, damit die Zuschauer direkt wissen, worum es geht. Menschen lieben Bilder und Videos und wollen weniger lesen.
Use 3‑5 seconds of a distinct, relevant visual motif for each spoken segment in Shorts; long videos may have longer demonstrations but must still align tightly with the narration.
A new motif must be a genuinely different visual (different subject, action, or tool view); zooms, crops, subtitle changes, decorative backgrounds, or minor label tweaks do not count.
Show the primary image, tool interface, or main subject prominently and clearly; never replace real screenshots or authentic UI views with symbolic illustrations or unrelated stock.
Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring them back for useful actions throughout; do not substitute channel figures with unrelated characters.
Include the mandatory spoken CTA (like, share, save) at the format‑specific position; do not replace it with a different call‑to‑action.
Place all on‑screen text, captions, and overlays within the inner title‑safe zone with sufficient padding to avoid clipping or overlap.
Maintain factual accuracy: never add unsupported specifications, performance guarantees, or invented details; resolve any unsupported‑detail warnings first.
Vary visual pacing by avoiding prolonged static shots; switch to dynamic, relevant visuals that illustrate the narration and keep the viewer engaged.
Craft a clear narrative arc: open with a compelling hook, develop the explanation, and provide a concrete, source‑backed answer before the CTA.
For AI‑Tools Explained, name each tool briefly then show authentic interface views and source‑supported examples; avoid generic stock or illustration substitutes.
Use the channel’s original painted open‑world aesthetic consistently for backgrounds, branding, and music, while ensuring each motif adds narrative value.
When a script calls for a concrete example or demo, include a brief, source‑supported walkthrough that visually demonstrates the described benefit.

skript.beschreibung: We read six official AI tool pricing pages on October 9, 2026 and summarized what each free plan includes and where paid plans begin. Check downloads, commercial rights and privacy before you publish.

belege.name: Looka (AI logo maker)
belege.text: "It's totally free to make logos. Only pay when you're happy!" Basic Logo Package: one low-res PNG file, $35 one-time purchase. Premium Logo Package: multiple high-res file types, $72 one-time purchase. Brand Kit Subscription: $96 per year. (Official page read on October 9, 2026.)

belege.name: Leonardo.Ai (image generator)
belege.text: Free plan: $0 per month, 150 fast tokens per day, creations access: Public. Essential plan: $12 per month, creations access: Private. (Official page read on October 9, 2026.)

belege.name: Gamma (AI presentations)
belege.text: Free plan: 400 credits at signup, create up to 10 slides per prompt. Plus plan adds 1,000 monthly credits and removes Gamma branding. (Official page read on October 9, 2026.)

belege.name: Suno (AI music)
belege.text: Free plan: 50 credits per day, no monthly song downloads, no commercial rights. Pro plan: 2,500 credits per month, commercial use rights. (Official page read on October 9, 2026.)

belege.name: ElevenLabs (AI voice)
belege.text: Free plan: $0 per month, 10k credits per month, text to speech. Commercial License and Instant Voice Cloning start with the paid Starter plan. (Official page read on October 9, 2026.)

belege.name: Notta (AI transcription)
belege.text: Free plan: 120 transcription minutes per month, up to 3 minutes per conversation. Pro plan: 1,800 minutes per month. (Official page read on October 9, 2026.)
